primary_paper.title: Sums and Differences of Finite Sets
primary_paper.relevant_location: Section 2, lemma preceding equation (11), definitions of s,d,q,theta; equations (13)-(15) define V(m,L), its counts, and projection weights.
primary_paper.finite_lemma: For a finite nonempty U of nonnegative integers containing 0, define s=|U+U|, d=|U-U|, q=2 max(U)+1 and theta=1+log(d/s)/log(q). The lemma explicitly assumes the strict condition d<q before concluding that there are finite integer-set pairs A,B of arbitrarily large |B| with a sumset bound and a difference-over-sumset exponent theta.
primary_paper.why_the_strict_condition_is_used: The strict inequality d<q is a stated hypothesis of the finite construction lemma. The checker enforces it exactly; equality is invalid.
primary_paper.scope: T080 maximizes the finite exponent parameter theta over a bounded family of U. It is not the T012 or T077 one-set score, and it is not itself the asymptotic conclusion of the theorem.

objective_distinction_examples.T012_vs_T080: For A={0,2,3,4,7,11,12,14} and B=A union (A+1000), both satisfy T012's s>d>n check and T080's d<q check. T012 ranks A above B, but T080 ranks B above A.
objective_distinction_examples.T077_vs_T080: For C=projection V(2,3) and D=projection V(18,1), both satisfy the T080 bounds. T077 ranks D above C, but T080 ranks C above D.

open_status.evidence: The cited lemma constructs asymptotic pairs from a finite U but does not prove that this U maximizes theta over the benchmark's bounded family. The small-set optimization for cardinality at most 11 does not settle the benchmark, which permits up to 512 elements.
open_status.limitation: The finite score is a certificate parameter from the lemma. It is not an optimality proof for the finite search domain.
